# Inflation cooled slightly to 3.4% in July

Core inflation, which strips out food and energy, climbed 0.2% for the month and 2.5% over the past year

By Cris Tolomia·2 min read·Updated August 12, 2026

Add QZ to Google

David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

The Consumer Price Index rose 0.1% in July on a seasonally adjusted basis, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Wednesday, pulling the annual inflation rate down to 3.4%, from 3.5% in June. # CPI report shows inflation eased in July to a 3.4% annual pace

Updated on: August 12, 2026 / 2:20 PM EDT
/ CBS News

Inflation eased for the second consecutive month, rising at a 3.4% annual pace in July, in line with economists' expectations and a signal that some consumer price pressures may be easing.

## By the numbers

Economists polled by the financial data firm FactSet predicted July inflation rose at an annual rate of 3.4%. [...] With the CPI cooling to a 3.5% annual pace in June, some economists say May could mark an inflationary peak for 2026, with some forecasting that inflation will continue to ease throughout the year.

Concerns about ongoing cyclospora outbreaks have dampened consumer demand for lettuce, which weighed on the index for fruits and vegetables.

Overall, the meats, poultry, fish and eggs index rose 1.9% over the 12 months ended in July, while the index for dairy fell 0.5% over the year.

The core CPI, which excludes food and energy, was up 2.5% on the year, with the indexes for new vehicles, apparel and shelter all notching modest increases. [...] Key Points
